Currently there is not an existing stand-alone degree program in NFS to prepare students for careers outside of the prescribed program for preparation of Registered Dietitian training.
In the past, students have found confusion around what to do with the Nutrition subplan outside of Dietetics due to the subplans under the same B.S. degree.
This stand alone degree will provide students who do not wish to pursue the RD credential a more clear degree pathway.
These students will examine how food and nutrition impacts systemic, biochemical and molecular health, the relationship to the food system and real world applications to physical and mental health.
The coursework in the NFS Nutrition degree is very well suited for a variety of post-baccalaureate careers as well as preparation for numerous graduate and post-professionals programs in health-care related fields and settings.
Eight of the top 15 most needed jobs according to indeed.com are health-related jobs, making it one of the desirable areas of study for both job security and income.

Graduates with this degree can find employment at major research centers, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, and nutraceutical industries, community nutrition programs, non-governmental organizations, the fitness industry and more.
A Nutrition degree can be the foundation for career opportunities in areas such as: Food and Nutrition Management, Public Health Nutrition, Education and Research, Consultant, Related Health Professionals (such as Chiropractor, Dentist, Naturopathic Doctor, Physical Therapist, Physician, Physician Assistant, Podiatrist, Veterinarian, and Nursing), Business and Industry, Media, International Food Organizations, Public Policy / Government.
This degree will have approximately 50% course work in Nutritional Sciences, dietetics and real-world health application with 50% course work in sciences, psychology and healthand science-related electives.
This suggested coursework will prepare students for direct job placement, further education in post-professional health related programs, research-based graduate programs or jobs related to nutrition and public health.

While developing the curriculum, the prerequisite courses were considered for a variety of programs to attempt to best prepare the students for moving forward and succeeding in their chosen career path.
